questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university offered some courses that I found interesting, and that it was a country outside Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best time of my life. I've never been outside of Scandinavia so it was amazing to finally experience something else. Montréal is not a big culture shock compared to Denmark, and I very quickly felt at home.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I spent alot of time preparing for my trip at home, and had some long e-mail 
correspondences with the University. Concordia also have a PDF guide for international students which was a big help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got an some e-mails, and besides that the university has a lot of happenings at the campus, where you can meet new people or ask other students about help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You have to actively reach out to people, no one was holding your hand.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was a member of the "KU-studerende i Canada" facebook group and saw someone mentioning a place called Cubahaus, it is housing for international students. I reached out to them and got a room in a two floor building with 6 other roomates. The house itself was not that good compared to Denmark standards, but I would definitely stay there again if I had the chance. It is very easy to find housing in Montréal in the winter just check facebook marketplace. If you are going in the summer I would look for housing months before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The quality of the houses/apartments can vary a lot. It's more expensive to live at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I spend alot of time writing e-mails to different people at the university, so definitely apply for your courses early on or else all the seats might be taken.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to use the student hub website, they have a course planer that is very helpful. The problem is if you want to apply for a course with prerequisites, you have to write to the professor in charge of the program.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
They have a lot of help on their website, and don't hesitate with writing an e-mail to the ISO (INTERNATIONAL
STUDENTS OFFICE) they answer e-mails fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as early as possible, then you will get the classes you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different compared to Denmark, but I really enjoyed it. You have small exams doing the hole semester instead of one big one in the end. It really helped keeping me engaged in the classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did elective courses at Concordia, and the level was very different depending on the class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You have to engage more actively in the classes, and do a lot more than just reading in books.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- BIOL 227 LAB STUDIES IN BIODIVERSITY
- FRAN 211 FRENCH LANGUAGE: ELEMENTARY
- PHIL 318 PHILOSOPHY OF BIOLOGY

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are into biology the lab course is very giving. You become very familiar with using a light compound microscope (something I feel like KU never tought me) and get to look at a lot of different organisms. Besides being in the lab you have to do three different surveys, which forces you to go out in nature and look for different organisms. I really enjoyed engaging with the outside nature as a part of my course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Do keep in mind that taxes aren't always included in the price so things are typically more expensive than you expect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is way cheaper compared to DK, get an OPUS card and then you pay 220 CAD for four months, you can take metro and bus as much as you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offer many event for intenational students and normal students. I participated in many free online workshops.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offer movie nights, game nights, to go watch hockey games, yoga lessons and lots more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Montréal is a city that offers so many free events. My stay was in the winter and I was so worried that I would just stay inside most of the time, but the people in Montréal do many outdoor activities despite the cold. If you are here in the winter go to the lumiere festival, the nuit blanche (it's like culture night in Denmark) and igloo festival.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I lived five minutes from place des arts where they have a skating rink, it is totally free if you have your own skates. I went there almost everyday in the morning where it opens, and there's only a few people. Go skate on the frozen river in parc la fontaine, discover Saint Laurent, go to Mont Royal and you have to experience tam tam in Parc du Mont-Royal if possible!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are so helpful and sweet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say hi! Montréal is a very diverse city and people here are very outgoing compared to Denmark

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their willingness to help out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for the quebec government health insurance (theres a guide on concordias website)
2. Go to the university in the beginning before classes start to participate in the happenings and meet new people.
3. Be open

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are not opening a bank account in Montréal you cannot pay for a phone subscription because they need an address. I was lucky I stayed at an airbnb in the beginning and the host was willing to pay for my subscription with her card and then I transferred the money to her. Fizz is very good.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own for the first time in my life in another country, but it was so fulfilling in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Live in the now, and enjoy the small things. As sad as it might be, you will meet people here that you might never see again, so enjoy the time you have with them as much as you can.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
